_comment: Recorded tool calls from live run run-20260926-235945-0uo6tt (claude-sonnet-5, s02). Orchestrator iteration 1 (role-named delegation) and maintenance iterations 5-10 (report attempts; non-FAA citations removed).

input.brief: A321 NW-PMC at PMI stand 14: catering high-loader platform struck lower frame of forward service door 1R. Evidence: dent ~8cm below sill, paint scuffed, one door-stop fitting looks displaced, door won't close flush, handle stiff, visible gap at bottom when closed. Please: (1) provide a provisional technical assessment of severity and likely MEL applicability for door 1R damage (cite the MEL item), (2) advise whether local B2 engineer Sol Larkstead (eng-pmi-b2, on site now) can perform any task here, or whether a B1/structures-qualified engineer is required to assess/certify - note nearest B1 engineers are Tamsin Pennick at MAN (eng-man-b1c, available now) and Fern Marshwood at AGP (eng-agp-b1, available from minute 90), (3) estimate repair vs inspection time if a B1 engineer is flown/positioned in, (4) flag this is a provisional read only - final airworthiness/MEL deferral decision rests with certifying staff.

PMI stand 14, A321 NW-PMC, door 1R damaged by catering truck high-loader. Need: (1) confirm truck/equipment withdrawn and secured, incident scene preserved for photos/handover, (2) status of stand 14 vs moving aircraft to remote stand R22 or contact stand 15 (occupied until minute 60) if needed for engineer access/inspection, (3) handler Tessaly Apron Services capacity to support (14 staff on shift, ack 6 min) - confirm they can support extended ground time / possible aircraft swap logistics (stairs, bus, gpu) if needed, (4) any other damage to fuselage/equipment from the strike.

NWD341 PMI-MAN 11:30 STD, 212 pax, A321 NW-PMC now AOG-suspect (door 1R damage, assessment in progress). Aircraft has 2 further sectors today (NWD342 MAN-ALC 15:00, NWD343 ALC-MAN 18:10). Spare A321 NW-MAT is available in Manchester (not Palma) from minute 0. Please assess: (1) rotation impact if NW-PMC is grounded for X minutes/hours - knock-on to NWD342/343, (2) feasibility/cost-benefit of positioning spare NW-MAT to cover downstream sectors vs waiting for repair, (3) crew duty margins for crew-341 (CPT Hana Ivesley, FO Tamsin Fenwright, SCCM Bram Kilnsey, 3 CC - all report 07:10, maxFdp 720min) if delay extends, and standby crew MAN (Lior Marshwood CPT, Teo Tollbridge FO) availability, (4) any options for swapping tails with NW-MAX rotation (NWD345/346) given both are on similar MAN-PMI routing today.

NWD341 PMI-MAN 11:30, 212 pax (166 general, 28 families with 11 infants, 3 PRM incl 1 WCHC, 15 with tight onward connections from MAN deadline 16:00). Aircraft NW-PMC has a door defect from ground equipment strike, under assessment; possible delay. Please draft an early holding message (AI-drafted, for human approval) to go out within 15 sim minutes: acknowledge a technical check is underway following a ground equipment issue, no confirmed delay length yet, reassure PRM/family passengers will be looked after, advise connection pax we are aware of their onward flights. Do not commit to a specific delay time or outcome yet.

Open and maintain the incident timeline log for NW-PMC door 1R strike at PMI. Log the trigger event (minute 5: catering high-loader contact with door 1R lower frame), evidence reports (handler supervisor account, photo-description of dent/scuff/displaced door-stop fitting, cabin crew report of stiff handle and visible gap), and flag that Palma is an outstation with only B2 licence coverage on site. Keep the log ready to receive maintenance/ground/flightops/passenger updates as they come in.

input.summary:
NW-PMC (A321, PMI stand 14) sustained ground-equipment contact damage to forward service door 1R (catering high-loader platform), ATA 32, logged as DEF-001, aircraft unserviceable. Evidence (8cm dent below sill, displaced door-stop fitting, stiff handle, visible gap, door not closing flush) indicates possible structural/rigging damage to the door frame/stop fitting, not a simple avionics or systems snag. This requires a B1 (structures) assessment and sign-off; the on-site engineer (Sol Larkstead) is B2-licensed (avionics) and cannot certify structural findings or clear this defect. Nearest B1 engineers are 275 min out (Tamsin Pennick, MAN, via positioning flight) or from minute 90 (Fern Marshwood, AGP, exact ETA to PMI not yet confirmed by the system). A damage-assessment work order is open but not yet confirmed as engineer-assigned in the system of record. No MEL item in the searched MMEL set covers frame/door-stop structural damage — MEL items found (52-30-01, 52-10-03, 52-10-04, 52-70-01) address actuator, exit-stop-fitting-for-unpressurised-ops, emergency-operation and ECAM-indication scenarios, not sill/frame impact damage — so MEL deferral is unlikely to be straightforwardly applicable pending inspection; this is my provisional read only, not a dispatch decision.</parameter>
<parameter name="actionsTaken">["Retrieved aircraft status and open defects for NW-PMC: DEF-001 open, ATA 32, door 1R, status unserviceable, no prior work orders/decisions.","Searched MEL/MMEL for door 1R / structural / frame damage and doors-chapter items generally; no item matches ground-impact structural/frame damage.","Searched ground-ops procedure literature on equipment contact and damage assessment before release (Airbus Safety First, CAP 642) confirming a structural damage assessment (SRM/ASR/ASRP or equivalent) is the expected process, not a MEL placard.","Paged B1 engineer Tamsin Pennick (MAN) — accepted, ETA minute 275 via positioning flight (arrives on NWD345 + 45 min).","Paged B2 engineer Sol Larkstead (PMI, on airport) — accepted, ETA minute 11 (7 min walk); note: this initial page was not tied to a work order id.","Attempted to page B1 engineer Fern Marshwood (AGP) and to re-page/assign Sol Larkstead to the work order — both calls errored (Fern busy until minute 90 and cannot be paged early; Sol already travelling so duplicate page rejected).","Opened work order WO-001-f96 (damage_assessment task, DEF-001, est. 120 min) — currently shows 0% progress and no confirmed engineer assignment in the aircraft record.","Drafted and got approval for a factual tech-log entry (TL-001-opn) documenting the strike, evidence, and assessment/work-order status, with unresolved checks listed.","Checked weather at PMI: sunny, 31°C, wind 9kt — no adverse-weather constraint on ground work or towing at this time."]
openIssues: Work order WO-001-f96 does not show a confirmed assigned engineer in the system record; need to re-page Sol Larkstead (or re-issue the work order paging call) explicitly bound to WO-001-f96 once he is on stand, and re-page Fern Marshwood at/after minute 90 with the work order id attached.

No B1 (structures/doors licensed) engineer is on-site or imminently available at PMI: earliest confirmed B1 options are Fern Marshwood (AGP, biddable from minute 90, PMI ETA not yet confirmed) or Tamsin Pennick (MAN, ETA minute 275) — both are materially later than the 11:30 STD of NWD341.

No MEL item found that covers frame/door-stop structural impact damage; applicability of any MEL deferral to DEF-001 is unconfirmed and, on the evidence (displaced door-stop fitting, frame dent), looks unlikely to be a simple placarded item — but this is a provisional read only.
Maintenance record for NW-PMC is Unknown for last check type/date and defect history — cannot rule out related prior door defects.
Full structural assessment (SRM-based), door rigging/lock-latch functional check, and check for hidden damage behind the sill/frame have not been performed.

Sol Larkstead (B2) can perform visual documentation and non-structural avionics/indication checks only; he cannot assess or certify the structural/door-stop damage — his findings would need B1 structural sign-off regardless.

Operational exposure: NWD341 (11:30 MAN, 212 pax) cannot realistically depart on schedule given no B1 engineer available before minute 90 at the earliest; downstream NWD342/NWD343 rotations and the MAN spare (NW-MAT) may need duty-manager consideration — outside maintenance authority to decide.
recommendations: Re-page Sol Larkstead (or confirm his existing page) explicitly against WO-001-f96 once he arrives on stand (~minute 11) to begin visual documentation, handle/latch inspection and photography, understanding this cannot substitute for B1 structural certification.
At minute 90, page Fern Marshwood (B1, AGP) against WO-001-f96 for structural assessment/certification of the door frame and door-stop fitting; confirm her PMI ETA once paged.

Do not treat any MEL item as authorising dispatch: none of the items found in this MMEL search addresses ground-impact structural/frame damage; a certifying (B1) engineer must complete a damage assessment (per manufacturer SRM/ASR guidance referenced in Airbus Safety First material) before any airworthiness or deferral decision.

Escalate to duty manager / network control now: given B1 ETA of at least minute 90 (unconfirmed exact PMI arrival) or minute 275, NWD341's 11:30 STD is very unlikely to be met on NW-PMC; consider the MAN-based spare NW-MAT and knock-on effects on NWD342/343 and the MAN crew/rotation — this is a scheduling decision for the duty manager, not maintenance.

Certifying B1 engineer to determine, after physical inspection, whether this is rectify, defer under an as-yet-unidentified MEL item, or AOG; record via record_engineering_decision once that assessment is complete — no decision has been taken yet.
